title: Prove all-field rigidity of shortest permutation circuits (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration. For every field K, permutation w in S_n and rank-one idempotent E, the exact formal endpoint `I+([w]-[e])E` has minimum adjacent-transposition call length `inv(w)`. Every normalized minimum word uses E at every call and its labels form a reduced expression for w. Arbitrarily many finite dirty spectators and free scalar GL mixing do not change this equality classification.

```text
shortest word => every right peel lowers the inversion cut
Grassmann equality => both scalar sides avoid spectators
one-dimensional active space => every paid projector equals E
```

Only `research/all-field-permutation-rigidity/` is added. Brian / JoyboyBrian's #4765 supplies binary S4 tight spectator elimination and its Grassmann method; Ross Richardson's #1989 supplies the ordered-pair cut and binary inversion tariff, retaining Adam Gall and the register-model lineage. Nick Petalas's #4851 already settles the all-field three-call S3 special case, including a larger coupling alphabet. The new result is the stated all-field, all-S_n equality classification in the idempotent alphabet. No predecessor scientific replay is a deliverable. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19362405). Scientific base and submission refresh are canonical main `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8, selected PR6030. The explicit scope change and historical pins are in TASK.json and SOURCES.json. Live claims, local reservations, recent account work, open and merged PR bodies, cached card coverage and main README searches were checked. Sparse notes, arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain coverage limits.

## Evidence

Before, the credited tight-peeling theorem was binary S4, and the credited all-field single-target theorem covered the S3 three-call case. After, PROOF.md proves the all-field, all-S_n classification without a finite search premise.

- All 18,792 ternary S4 peeling cases pass. There are 468 decreasing peels, each with the endpoint projector and a right descent. Two-register endpoints and calls range over all 12 rank-one idempotents; three-register calls range over all 117 with endpoint E00.
- Complete coefficientwise endpoints and a separate regular-action calculation pass for 46 nonidentity S4 fixtures over Q and F3, on all 2,760 basis columns. The first example has four inversions and a rational oblique three-register projector.
- Four call omissions, four changed projectors and three boundary controls pass. The boundary controls include a longer valid word that uses spectators and a one-call implementation when a nonsimple target label is allowed.
- Local CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, standard library only: direct normal 0.96s, direct optimized 0.86s, complete registered replay 1.90s. Both VERIFY.json commands have 60-second timeouts. Ordinary and optimized generated receipts agree, including source hashes.
- `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` pass. The publication preflight checks all six committed files and the declared source ancestry. The worktree is clean.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/all-field-permutation-rigidity
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/all-field-permutation-rigidity/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/all-field-permutation-rigidity/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/all-field-permutation-rigidity --check-source-history
```

Other installations can substitute their CPython 3.12 executable. Direct runs are read-only and print `PASS_ALL_FIELD_PERMUTATION_RIGIDITY` in a generated JSON receipt bound to all six package hashes. No receipt is handwritten.

## Limitations

This is a scoped formal algebraic theorem, not a native supplier, improved kappa or complete multiplication theorem. The statement requires adjacent labels, rank-one idempotents, one active line, full dirty restoration and minimum unweighted length. Higher-rank targets, nonidempotent couplings and arbitrary separate label prices are unclassified. Native scalar charges, frames, hosting, ownership, precision, stock, tape and the complete recursive bill remain unprovided. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Lean, Docker and the selected scientific cold replay were not run. The selected frontier is unchanged.

## Open next questions

For a rank-two endpoint over a nonbinary field, classify minimum words inside its active plane. Start with one S4 endpoint and exact two-dimensional coefficient equations. The present one-dimensional idempotence conclusion does not provide that classification or a physical price.

## Related open work

- [#3893](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3893) prices one binary three-register S3 target tuple. This theorem classifies a single active line over every field and computes no new value for that tuple.
- [#6408](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6408) gives cocycle rank floors for split normal-subgroup alphabets. This package uses ordered-pair Grassmann equality and computes none of its normal-subgroup tariffs.
- [#6403](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6403) gives quotient-loop rigidity and weighted two-normal-target tariffs in binary semilinear groups. The endpoint, alphabet, coefficient-field scope and proof method here differ; no numerical comparison is asserted.
- [#6383](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6383) classifies alternating lattice-descent words in characteristic two. Its Laurent-label parity question differs from this adjacent-permutation geodesic classification.

- [#6441](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6441), opened after the CLAIM, proves defining-characteristic faithfulness widths for point-column group-algebra actions. This package keeps full formal permutation equality and uses a necessary ordered-pair image; it computes none of those width thresholds.
- [#6442](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6442), opened after the CLAIM, prices inserted rank-one linear repairs for an ordinary wrapper. Its linear correction alphabet and endpoint differ from the formal adjacent-permutation word here; no common numerical quantity is computed.

The completion refresh read this account's open PRs created since the advance CLAIM. None studies this exact shortest single-permutation endpoint, and none reports a competing value computed here. No additional computations were run to check other PRs.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated. Six new files in one opt-in package; no shared source or frozen evidence changes.
